## review-until-clean, pass 1

**Review:** `code-review medium --max-findings all origin/main...HEAD`. It returned 3 candidates (not cut short) and no correctness bugs.

**Head started from:** `cb9a618c95bf68358e7173d04ffa301227244d7c`
**Head pushed:** no push. This pass changed nothing, so the head is still `cb9a618c`.

### Is the bump complete?
- **Every place the version is pinned moved.** The constitution names two homes for the pin: `.specify/init-options.json` (`speckit_version`) and `SPECKIT_SUPPORTED_VERSION` in `.github/actions/wing-commander-preflight/action.yml`. Both say `1.1.2`. `integration.json` and both manifests also say `1.1.2`. I grepped the repo outside `specs/`: no other file, gates under `.github/scripts/` included, restates the old version.
- **Manifest hashes match the files.** I recomputed every sha256 listed in `claude.manifest.json` and `speckit.manifest.json`. All match the files on disk, with no mismatch and no missing file.
- **Upstream v1.1.2 changed nothing this repo vendors.** I diffed upstream `v1.1.0..v1.1.2`. It shows **no changes under `templates/` or `scripts/`**, which are the sources of the vendored `.claude/skills/speckit-*` and `.specify/` files. The changes are in the CLI, the MCP server, catalog versions and tests. So a diff that only changes version strings is the correct, complete result. The local customisations of the vendored skills have nothing new to absorb.

### Candidates
| # | Verdict | Location | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Out of scope | `.github/workflows/auto-update-spec-kit.yml:1653` | The #191 post-condition counts any change under `.specify/` as proof that the upgrade ran, and the stamps in `integration.json` and the manifests count too. So a hypothetical partial upgrade that rewrites only the stamps would pass. The guard's stated target is the no-op path where the manifest is missing, and that path writes no stamps. Either way, this PR doesn't touch that file. |
| 2 | Refuted | `.specify/integrations/speckit.manifest.json:4` | `installed_at` stayed at 2026-07-04 while `version` moved. This is upstream behaviour: `integration upgrade` updates `installed_at` only when it rewrites files, and none of the speckit files changed. No gate reads it, and hand-editing generated bookkeeping would make it wrong. |
| 3 | Refuted | `.github/actions/wing-commander-preflight/action.yml:134` | The preflight check is an exact match, so adopters still on 1.1.0 will get a warning. This is by design: constitution §Governance says the pin is exact and moved by the auto-update stage, and the check only warns and never fails (research.md D7). |

### Fixes and tests
None. No candidate was real and in scope.

### Gates
`run-local-gates.py --jobs 4` on `cb9a618c`: **271/273 passed**. The two failures are `verify-gate-62.py` and `verify-gate-62.py --self-test`, waived because they need Docker and there is no Docker socket in this cloud session (`failed to connect to the docker API at unix:///var/run/docker.sock`).

### Out of scope
- `auto-update-spec-kit.yml` #191 post-condition: the stamp files written by the upgrade (`integration.json` and the `version`/`installed_at` fields in `.specify/integrations/*.manifest.json`) satisfy the "changed a Spec Kit artifact" check. The guard could compare the manifests' `files` maps instead.

**CLEAN**

⚠️ **Not fully converged — 17 tasks remain**

This specification lets one repository hold several independent Wing Commander projects as folders (nodes), nested to any depth within a 28-character path cap. A maintainer routes an issue to a folder with a `node:<path>` label, and intake, clarify, plan, tasks, implement, finalize, rebase, pr-conversation and cleanup then run the whole lifecycle inside that folder with its own constitution, `.specify/`, spec-kit skills and `specs/`. Routing is an optional intake input that defaults to empty, so a repository without it keeps today's root behaviour, names and numbering.

The shared logic has one home. `_shared/project-name.sh` holds the path grammar, folder checks, name parsing, slug budget and per-project numbering, and a `wing-commander-project` composite exposes it to the workflows. Project-aware versions of the spec-meta, preflight, context, write-boundary, fold-queue, checkbox-count and stage-findings actions now take a repository-relative spec directory, and the root outputs are kept byte-identical. Numbering is per project, and intake, per-spec and cleanup concurrency and label names are scoped to the project, so two projects can both produce `001-login` without collisions.

Subfolder agents are contained to their folder. A pre-push hook, a post-agent containment check against a trusted default-branch base, a re-checkout of the pipeline composites after the agent step, and a stale-folder re-check together keep agent-authored changes inside the project. The tool-args composite adds the `.claude/` denies for the root and each enclosing project, and the pipeline-checkout guard refuses any branch that tracks `.wing-commander-pipeline/`. Label-first creation of `spec:P/<NNN-slug>` happens before the first branch push, and a re-run refusal and per-issue serialization stop a second routed intake for the same issue. New gate checks cover path grammar, name parsing, numbering, containment, routing, root compatibility, graduation by copy and the single-home rule, with fixtures under `.github/scripts/fixtures/`. The branch is 114 commits ahead of `origin/main`, touching 87 files (about 9,350 lines added). Most tasks are checked, but the spec is not finished: final validation, the root byte-identity review, the constitution amendment (T056, a separate human-merged PR), and a full gate-suite run are still open.

Code review of #1022 at `87ae553`. This is in-scope review feedback on this spec. Five fresh-session reviewers each covered one area (root compatibility, security, spec conformance, wiring, gates), and an adversarial pass verified every finding. Please fold this in and fix it on this branch, in this order. Lint is currently red on Gate 12 and Gate 60.

### Blocker

1. **The containment check fails every subfolder stage** (`wing-commander-containment/action.yml:45`). `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` lists the untracked trusted checkout `.wing-commander-pipeline/`, which is outside `P`. So intake, clarify, plan, tasks, implement, finalize and the pr-conversation act stage all fail after their agent step, even when the agent touched only `P`.
   - In the composite, exclude only the root checkout from the untracked listing, with an anchored pathspec: `-- ':/' ':(exclude,top).wing-commander-pipeline'`. Don't use an unanchored `--exclude`, which would also hide `P/.wing-commander-pipeline`. Leave the two `git diff` legs unfiltered, so a committed gitlink is still flagged.
   - Also append `/.wing-commander-pipeline/` to `.git/info/exclude` after the consumer checkout. That closes #1030.
   - Add a Gate 160 case: an untracked nested git repo at `.wing-commander-pipeline/` with a change only inside `P` must pass.

### Major

2. **Gate 12** fails because `_shared/intake-pre-push.sh` calls `gh` (lines 65 and 67).
   - The hook should only validate (ref shape, allocated number, slug budget, containment) and record the validated slug, for example in a file under `$RUNNER_TEMP`.
   - A deterministic post-agent step in intake, or `wing-commander-publish-stranded-commits` through its `label-first-*` inputs, then creates the `spec:P/<slug>` label, adds it to the issue, and pushes with hardening, all under a declared token.
   - For routed intake, deny `Bash(git push --no-verify:*)` and `Bash(git push -n:*)`, so label-first can't be bypassed (FR-014).
3. **Gate 60:** published workflows reach into `_shared` directly at `pr-conversation.yml:2225`, `rebase.yml:1022` and `intake.yml:754-756`. Intake slips past the gate's regex through a `shared=` variable.
   - Add composite modes on `wing-commander-containment`: `install-pre-push` (copies the helpers from `$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/../_shared`, writes the hook, sets `core.hooksPath`) and `filter` (rebase's manifest).
   - Route all three call sites through them.
   - Widen the gate to catch the variable indirection.
4. **Rename bypass:** `git diff --name-only` reports only a rename's destination, so moving a file from outside `P` into `P` passes. Add `--no-renames` to both diff legs. Add reject fixtures for a committed move, a staged move, and a delete outside `P` paired with a near-identical add inside `P`.
5. **Pre-push containment and a cumulative guard.** The self-pushing subfolder agents (clarify, plan auto and pr, tasks auto and pr, implement cycle and retry, finalize) have no containment pre-push hook. The post-agent guard only diffs this run, so a violation pushed earlier survives a restart.
   - Install the hook before each of these agents (item 3's composite mode).
   - Make the guard also diff from `git merge-base origin/<default-branch> HEAD`.
6. **FR-006:** subfolder agents still read the root constitution, because the skills read `.specify/memory/constitution.md` relative to the root.
   - Add a deterministic project paragraph, like intake's, to the clarify, plan, tasks, implement, finalize and pr-conversation act prompts. It points reads at `P/.specify/memory/constitution.md`, `P/.specify/extensions.yml` and `P/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
   - Gate that every project-wired prompt carries the paragraph.
7. **FR-023:** intake's real `findings-label-prefix` never reaches the overlap check (`project-name.sh:161`), so `found-by:` is accepted.
   - Add a `findings-label-prefix` input to `wing-commander-project` and pass it from intake.
   - Drive Gate 162 through that input, not a raw environment variable, and add a `found-by:` reject case.
8. **FR-005:** clarify's preflight (`clarify.yml:425`) and both pr-conversation preflights (around `:603` and `:1857`) still check the root.
   - Resolve the project first and pass `project:` to each preflight.
   - Gate that every `require-speckit: "true"` preflight in a project-wired job passes `project:`.
9. **FR-007:** the stage-findings spec-document and contract classifier (`wing-commander-stage-findings/action.yml:252`) is root-only. Recognise `P/specs/NNN-…` and `P/specs/*/contracts/`, with fixtures.
10. **Wrong spec PR for a subfolder lifecycle:** intake finds the spec PR by `$SPEC_DRAFT_PREFIX$NUM-` (`intake.yml:1607`). For a subfolder lifecycle that can match a root PR with the same number.
    - Expose the exact branch from 'Resolve created spec' and use `gh pr list --head "$BRANCH"`.
    - Add a gate case.

### Minor

11. **Merge commits:** `containment.sh:51` ignores merge commits. Use `git log --format= --name-only --no-renames -c …`, and add an evil-merge fixture.
12. **pr-conversation act** keeps `Bash(gh api:*)` under the bot token for subfolder lifecycles, which is a contents-API write path around containment. Subtract it in `wing-commander-tool-args` when the project is non-empty, re-granting only the endpoints the act routes need. If that isn't feasible, record it as an accepted gap in `contracts/containment-and-trusted-checkout.md`.
13. **`check-folder` real-entry rule:** test every component (`.specify/memory`, `.specify/scripts`, each `SKILL.md`) for symlinks. Add fixtures for a symlinked memory dir, a symlinked skills dir and a symlinked skill file.
14. **Routing resolution must refuse, not fall back to the root:**
    - a bare routing label (`node:`) refuses instead of routing to the root;
    - a failed `gh issue view` read refuses instead of routing to the root;
    - the parser rejects a leading `/` or `//` instead of normalising it;
    - `-iterN` is stripped only for implement branches.
    Add fixtures for each.
15. **T066, widened:** replace every remaining inline project/slug split, including `read-spec-meta.sh` and the plan, tasks and rebase sites, with `project-name.sh parse`. Anchor rebase's `ls-remote` to `refs/heads/${SPEC_PREFIX}`.
16. **Stale-folder re-check:** add it after checkout in pr-conversation act and act.fold, rebase and cleanup.
17. **Stranded claim label:** the routing gate's `spec-intake-claimed` claim is stranded when a pending intake is cancelled. Add a `release-claim` job with `if: always()` and no concurrency group.
18. **Root byte-identity (FR-016):**
    - the root intake prompt gains blank lines around `routing-notes`;

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Action needed: Answer the open clarification questions**
>
> ## Question 1
> 
> **Context**: FR-001 (Project resolution). GitHub only reads workflows from the root .github/workflows/, so per-project wrappers would all sit side by side there. Whatever is chosen, the project path is untrusted input validated by deterministic code (FR-002) and recorded once in the lifecycle's durable identity (FR-003).
> 
> **What we need to know**: How does an issue name the project (subfolder) its lifecycle runs in?
> 
> **Suggested Answers**:
> 
> | Option | Answer | Implications |
> |--------|--------|--------------|
> | A | A label such as node:<path> applied alongside spec-request | GitHub-native and visible on the issue; needs one label per project (or a dynamic label); label names have a length limit that deep paths may hit. |
> | B | A field in the issue form | No label sprawl; the routing step has to parse it from the issue body, which is untrusted text, so validation must be strict; issues filed without the form need a fallback. |
> | C | A separate wrapper set per project, each passing a fixed project path as a stage input | Simplest routing logic and no parsing; wrapper count grows linearly with projects in the root .github/workflows/, and adding a project means adding wrappers. |
> | Custom | Provide your own answer | Reply on this issue with your own answer |
> 
> **Your choice**: _Reply on this issue_
> 
> ## Question 2
> 
> **Context**: FR-009 / FR-010 / FR-012 (Feature numbering). Either way the project's own specs/ is always scanned so teardown can't cause a reissue.
> 
> **What we need to know**: Should feature numbers run per project or come from one repository-wide sequence?
> 
> **Suggested Answers**:
> 
> | Option | Answer | Implications |
> |--------|--------|--------------|
> | A | Per project, each starting at 001 | Matches Spec Kit, keeps a graduated project's history clean, lets the intake concurrency group become per project; requires a project key in labels, branches and concurrency groups. |
> | B | One sequence shared across the repository | NNN-slug stays unique repo-wide so names need less namespacing; intake stays serialized across all projects; existing adopters' overlapping numbers (both have 001-013) cannot be moved in unchanged. |
> | Custom | Provide your own answer | Reply on this issue with your own answer |
> 
> **Your choice**: _Reply on this issue_
> 
> ## Question 3
> 
> **Context**: FR-011 / FR-014 (Isolation and names). Branch prefixes are already per-call stage inputs, but watchdog reads repo-wide WING_COMMANDER_*_PREFIX variables, fold-cycle-guard uses defaults, and preflight rejects '/' inside a prefix.
> 
> **What we need to know**: How are branches, spec: labels and concurrency groups namespaced for a subfolder project?
> 
> **Suggested Answers**:
> 
> | Option | Answer | Implications |
> |--------|--------|--------------|
> | A | One project key derived deterministically from the folder path, prefixing branches, labels and concurrency groups together | One source of truth that watchdog and fold-cycle-guard can derive without wrapper inputs; needs a collision-checked normalisation of paths (and either flattening '/' or relaxing preflight's prefix check). |
> | B | Separately configurable inputs per piece (branch prefixes, label prefix, concurrency prefix), as branch prefixes are today | Maximum flexibility for wrappers; every repository-wide consumer (watchdog, fold-cycle-guard, cleanup) must learn every project's configuration, and pieces can drift out of agreement. |
> | Custom | Provide your own answer | Reply on this issue with your own answer |
> 
> **Your choice**: _Reply on this issue_

🐕 **Wing Commander · watchdog** — run passed inspection on 9 of 10 evidence collectors (1 collector(s) errored; their evidence classes were not examined). _[Inspected run](https://github.com/charlesguse/wing-commander/actions/runs/38489901036)_

**Q1: A** — a maintainer applies `node:<path>` before or together with `spec-request`. The prefix is a new optional intake input that defaults to empty (routing off).

**Q2: A** — number per project, each starting at 001.

**Q3: Custom** — the key is the validated folder path itself, unchanged, placed after the existing flat prefixes. No flattening, hashing or per-piece inputs.

**Q1.** Only triage+ users can apply labels, so routing carries the same authority as entry. A form field stays author-editable after approval. Per-project wrappers can't split the repo-wide watchdog, cleanup, rebase or fold-cycle-guard triggers. Making the prefix opt-in keeps root adopters byte-identical.
- Intake reads live labels through `issue-number`, never the event payload or the body. Zero routing labels means root, one means that project, two or more means refuse with a callout and create nothing.
- Deterministic code validates the path before use: segments `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$` joined by `/`, no `specs` segment, no segment matching `^[0-9]{3}-`, and a real directory (no symlinks) on the default branch with `.specify/` and `.claude/skills/speckit-*`. Invalid paths are rejected, never normalised.
- Only intake reads the routing label. Every other stage, plus watchdog and fold-cycle-guard, takes the project from the recorded identity (branch, `spec:` label, spec-dir dispatch data). Later label changes have no effect. Re-running intake on an issue that already has a `spec:` label refuses.

**Q2.** sand-game (001–019) and recess-rocks (001–013) move in without renumbering, graduated copies continue their own sequence, and this matches Spec Kit.
- For project P, the next number is 1 plus the highest NNN in `P/specs/` and in refs exactly matching `refs/heads/<spec-draft|spec prefix>P/<NNN-slug>` (anchored). The root counts only remainders without `/`.
- Intake concurrency: the root keeps `wing-commander-intake`, and project P uses `wing-commander-intake/P`.

**Q3.** Strictly validated paths are injective, so no collision search is needed. Preflight's `/` rule stays, and repo-wide consumers read the project from names they already parse.
- The root key is empty, so every root name, number and spec-meta stays exactly as today.
- Branches: `<prefix>P/<NNN-slug>`, `<impl-prefix>P/<NNN-slug>-iterN`. Label: `spec:P/<NNN-slug>`. Spec dir: `P/specs/<NNN-slug>`. Per-spec group: `wing-commander-<spec dir>`.
- Labels are capped at 50 characters, and `spec:` + P + `/` + NNN-slug must fit, so P + NNN-slug ≤ 44. Deterministic code, not the prompt, gives the agent the slug budget, checks it, and creates the label before any branch exists. Over budget fails, never truncates. Paths over 28 characters are refused, leaving at least 16 for NNN-slug. That caps path length, not depth.
- spec-meta.json stays project-relative (`specs/<NNN-slug>`) and never records P. FR-003's durable record is the branch, `spec:` label and dispatch identity, not spec-meta, which keeps FR-008 (graduation by copy) intact.
- One shared parser: strip the prefix or `spec:`, the last segment is the slug, the rest is P. Branch listing and deletion use anchored full refnames.

Spec review of #1021. Please fold these changes into the spec. The three earlier answers stand. These items fix inconsistencies and gaps and settle four follow-on decisions. **Decisions** 1. **Root adopters stay byte-identical.** The re-run refusal (intake on an issue that already has a `spec:` label), label-first creation in deterministic code, and the slug-budget check apply only when the routing prefix is set. With routing off, intake behaves exactly as today. FR-016 and SC-003 stay unconditional. 2. **Write scope.** A subfolder lifecycle's agent-authored changes are confined to `P`. SC-001, Story 1's Independent Test and AS-1.2 all say this, with no "where legitimately required" clause. Whether deterministic code or the deny list enforces it is a plan decision. Any guard must still allow whole-folder operations and parent-index edits, which some adopters' constitutions permit. 3. **Per-project Spec Kit pinning.** Preflight's version-drift warning reads the resolved project's `.specify/init-options.json`. auto-update-spec-kit regenerating per-project copies is out of scope; state that. 4. **`spec_branch` in spec-meta keeps the real branch name** as a historical pointer. FR-008's no-`P` rule governs `spec_dir`, which is the identity field. No check may require `spec_branch` to resolve after teardown or graduation. **Terms and identity** 5. Define two terms and use them everywhere: **repository-relative** spec dir = `P/specs/` (dispatch data, concurrency, metrics); **project-relative** = `specs/` (spec-meta, paths handed to Spec Kit or the agent inside `P`). Fix FR-007, FR-019, AS-1.1, AS-1.3, Clarifications and the Spec directory entity. 6. State the self-identity rule: `P/specs//spec-meta.json` must record exactly `specs/`, and a record that carries any project path fails. Add a node pass/fail scenario, plus the same files passing after copy-out (Story 4). 7. Every slug-shaped carrier takes the project-qualified form `P/`, parsed by the shared parser: the plan→tasks `slug` hand-off and the plan/tasks manual-restart `slug` inputs. Root values stay unchanged. Add this to FR-003 and the Lifecycle identity entity. 8. FR-013's shared parser covers each name type, including stripping `-iterN` from implement branches. Rename the Key Entity "Project key" to "Project path (used verbatim)", and reword Story 5 AC2 so it no longer says the key is "derived". **Wrappers (FR-018 rewrite)** 9. A multi-project repository keeps **one shared wrapper set**. The guide documents: (a) setting the intake routing-prefix input; (b) widening the plan path filter, and the tasks path filter in `pr` review mode, to match every project's `specs/` at any depth, because otherwise a node's spec-PR merge never starts plan; (c) one `node:` label per project; (d) the project-qualified restart slug. Remove "select one project's changes" from FR-018 and "(however routing works)" from the Assumption. **Security and containment** 10. New FR: for a lifecycle in `P`, the agent's Edit/Write denies cover the root `.claude/`, the repository `.git/`, `P/.claude/` and the `.claude/` of projects nested inside `P`, whatever the working directory. This holds under the default `no-write-paths` and under any override, and still comes from the single no-write-paths definition (spec 090). Add subfolder and nested accept/reject fixtures. 11. FR-002/FR-005: `P`'s `.specify/`, `.claude/` (including the speckit skills), `specs/` and constitution must be real entries inside `P`, not symlinks. Add reject fixtures. 12. When the routing prefix is set, validate it: its format; no overlap with pipeline label families (`spec:`, `stage:`, `model:`, the findings and write-boundary prefixes); and a length that leaves room for a 28-character path within 50 characters. Add it to FR-019. 13. Any spec-number collision or uniqueness check, today the watchdog's spec-collision collector, is scoped to the inspected lifecycle's project. The same `NNN` in another project is never flagged. Add it to FR-019. **Completeness** 14. FR-007: add the deterministic code that classifies a file path as a spec document or contract. FR-020: widen the gate to `.github/actions/**` (including `_shared/`) as well as stage workflows. 15. Budget: slug ≤ `44 − len(P)` for a subfolder project. The root keeps today's behaviour (decision 1). Qualify FR-004 as "any depth within the 28-character path cap", and drop "unbounded" from the Assumption. 16. Edge case: if the recorded project folder no longer exists, or is no longer a Spec Kit project, on the ref a stage works from (for example after a move or rename mid-lifecycle), the stage fails loudly naming the folder and never writes to the stale path. Numbering does not reconcile refs under a former path. 17. Assumption: agent instruction files from enclosing projects (parent `CLAUDE.md`, root `.claude/settings`) may reach a subfolder agent. Excluding them is out of scope, the guide mentions it, and planning confirms how claude-code-action and skill discovery behave with a subfolder working directory. 18. Add a scenario for the mixed topology: routing on, FR-018 wrappers, and a root lifecycle and a subfolder lifecycle with the same `NNN-slug` running concurrently. The root's names, groups and numbering match today's, and neither cleanup touches the other's refs or labels. **Edits and structure** 19. Promote the constitution amendment to an FR (modelled on spec 110 FR-003). It names every clause to change: Principle VI's artifact path list, Principle V's `.claude/` scope (item 10), and the Operational Constraints spec-path and branch-convention bullets (`[

/]`, `[

/]-iterN`). It states the version bump and that the amendment is human-merged. 20. Add a Layer statement naming both Principle VII layers. The new intake input is a deliberate, optional widening of the published contract. 21. AS-1.1's Given sets the routing prefix to `node:`. Its Then names the spec-draft branch `ideas/alpha/`, since intake creates only that branch. 22. Restate preflight's prefix rule as it actually is (a single segment ending in exactly one `/`). Line 107's paths fail FR-002's grammar; they are not "invalid in branch names". 23. Edge case on root and nested scope: say "nested projects' *contents*" are out of an enclosing lifecycle's scope, and that the adopter's constitution defines that boundary.

## Plan complete: 114-subfolder-project-lifecycles

**Summary.** A lifecycle names its project `P` once, at intake, through a maintainer-applied `node:<path>` label. The label prefix is a new optional intake input, `routing-label-prefix`, default empty. Deterministic code validates `P` and records it in the branch, `spec:` label and repository-relative spec directory names. Every later stage, the watchdog and the fold-cycle guard recover `P` through one shared parser. Nothing is re-inferred.

- **Single home.** New `_shared/project-name.sh` (grammar, parser, budget, numbering) and a `wing-commander-project` composite. Preflight, context, spec-meta, write-boundary and the fold-queue actions become project-aware.
- **Containment.** Project-derived `.claude/` and `.git/` denies join the single `no-write-paths` definition via `tool-args`. A new post-agent `wing-commander-containment` diff guard fails any change outside `P`.
- **Trusted checkout.** All `.wing-commander-pipeline/` and repository-tooling references become workspace-root absolute paths. A tracked `.wing-commander-pipeline/` at any depth is refused.
- **Intake.** Per-project numbering, label-first creation with a slug budget, re-run refusal when routing is on, and a per-issue gate job for race safety.
- **Gates.** Seven new `verify-*.py` gates with accept/reject fixtures.

**Artifacts** (in `specs/114-subfolder-project-lifecycles/`): plan.md, research.md, data-model.md, quickstart.md, contracts/project-path-and-names.md, contracts/routing-and-intake.md, contracts/containment-and-trusted-checkout.md, spec-meta.json (stage: plan).

**Constitution check:** passed with no unjustified violations. Principles V and VI and the Operational Constraints need the planned FR-024 amendment (2.4.0 to 2.5.0). It ships as a separate human-merged PR that must reach `main` no later than the lifecycle PR (research D12).

Spec 114, Subfolder Project Lifecycles (lifecycle issue #1020), merged as a101aace (finalize PR #1022), lets one repository hold several independent Wing Commander projects as folders. A maintainer applies a `node:<path>` label to route an issue to a subfolder project; intake then runs the lifecycle inside that folder, with its own constitution, `.specify/`, spec-kit skills and `specs/`. Root-level adopters are unchanged: routing is off by default and the root names, labels, concurrency groups and numbering stay the same.

The merge adds deterministic project-path validation, a shared name parser, per-project feature numbering, and project-qualified branch, label and concurrency-group names. It also adds containment and trusted-checkout guards that confine agent writes to the project folder, plus new composite actions (`wing-commander-project`, `wing-commander-containment`, `wing-commander-label-first`) and several new verification gates with checked-in fixtures. Its 87 changed files add about 9,350 lines and remove about 300.

## Summary

Draft spec `specs/115-board-loop-self-merge/` for the board loop performing the two bot merge classes constitution Principle X already authorizes:

- **Fix-PR merge (P1)**: when every condition holds on a freshly fetched snapshot of the exact head SHA (checks green with the gate suite run on that SHA, the independent review at zero open findings, the backstop holding on the final diff, the kill switch clear), the loop squash-merges at that SHA and posts an announcement naming each condition's result.
- **Dependency-bump merge (P2)**: a Spec Kit upgrade the auto-update stage opened, merged by the board loop once its assigned verification passed and the gate suite is green on the exact head. The backstop does not apply to this class.
- **Refusal handover (P2)**: a merge GitHub refuses, including a workflow-touching PR the App can't merge, goes to a maintainer with the reason stated. The loop never reaches `main` another way.
- **Prove (P3)**: when a merged change only runs in Actions, the loop re-drives one run and records the evidence on the merged PR (through spec 096's prove entry).

The new behaviour sits behind its own switch, off by default. While the switch is off, readiness behaves exactly as it does today. Spec, plan and lifecycle PRs, and constitution amendments, are out of scope.

**Open questions:** none. All clarifications are resolved (see the owner's answer on #903): FR-006 now names one switch, `WING_COMMANDER_BOARD_AUTO_MERGE` (default off), for both merge classes, with the existing `WING_COMMANDER_BOARD_LOOP_PAUSED` as its kill switch.

This specification lets the board loop merge its own bot-authored pull requests, in two classes that constitution Principle X already authorizes: the bounded fix-PR class, and the verified dependency-bump class (a Spec Kit upgrade opened by the auto-update stage). The merge is off by default and sits behind one switch, `WING_COMMANDER_BOARD_AUTO_MERGE`, with the existing `WING_COMMANDER_BOARD_LOOP_PAUSED` as the kill switch. Every merge condition is re-derived from a freshly fetched snapshot of the exact head SHA, and the merge call pins that SHA with `--match-head-commit`, so a head that moved between evaluation and merge is refused and nothing reaches `main`.

The decision logic lives in one place, `.github/scripts/board_merge.py`. It defines the fix-class and bump-class condition tuples, reuses the existing readiness checks for green checks and the gate suite, excludes spec, plan, lifecycle and constitution PRs from eligibility, and classifies GitHub merge refusals. A new gate, `verify-board-merge.py`, requires a checked-in fixture for every merge-blocking condition and refusal class, asserts the workflow's merge invariants (no `--admin`, no `--auto`, no second merge method), and checks that the merge job's `if:` carries both switch variables. The constitution parity gate now also requires the new switch name in both the constitution and `board-loop.yml`.

In `board-loop.yml` a new `merge` job runs after `select` and `readiness`. It re-checks the kill switch and the switch variable, gathers the fresh snapshot, and merges only when the decision says so. It announces the head SHA, class and each condition's result on the PR and the issue. A refused merge is classified, posted as a handover naming the maintainer, and recorded with a `handed-over` marker so the item is not retried every hour. The auto-update workflow now posts a `wc-bump-verification` record bound to the upgrade PR's head SHA and never merges its own PR. Merged items carry a `merged` marker with the merge SHA, which the existing prove-gate path picks up without a second eligibility classifier.

The branch has been through five review-gate rounds, and many of their findings are fixed and checked off in tasks.md. Several are still open, including unrecognised merge failures being classed as permanent refusals, the empty merge SHA case, the marker round and field carry-over, the forgeable bump verification record, and the auto-update step closing its PR on persistent comment failure. The post-merge proof re-drive (T033) has not run, and the switch is meant to stay unset until the refusal handover and the fix-class path have both landed.

## Spec 115 finished locally after the implement cap (head 30b3e1a)

The implement stage stopped at its 5-cycle cap with 13 tasks open, so this was finished in a local session on `spec/115-board-loop-self-merge`. Five commits went on top of 94f63b5: bf34c42, a083688, 0b40f48, 2a13d8c, 30b3e1a. Every open task is checked off except T033, the post-merge proof, which stays a maintainer step.

### Review gate round 1: the 8 findings (PR #1059 at 608c3e26)

Each fix has a test that fails on the old code and passes on the new. I checked this by running the new gate and tests against the pre-fix files.

1. **The "Not merged" dedup piped `gh api` into `grep -q` under pipefail.** Fixed. The pipe is gone. Every announcement now ends with a `wc-board-merge-outcome` marker (head_sha, class, outcome, reason). `board_merge.py announce` prints nothing when the PR's fresh snapshot already has that exact record from the App, so nothing is piped into grep. Test: `verify-board-merge.py` fails a merge job that pipes `gh … | grep -q` (with a self-test case) and unit-tests `already_announced`.
2. **A refused bump PR got no marker, so it was retried and re-announced every run.** Fixed. A `refused` outcome marker on the PR means `handed_over_at_head()`, and `pick_bump_candidate` skips that PR until its head moves (FR-010). A new push makes it a candidate again. Test: unit checks in the gate for refused-at-head, skipped, and released once the head moves.
3. **`pick_bump_candidate` let one stuck PR hide newer valid ones.** Fixed. The merge job now snapshots every auto-update-shaped open PR. `pick_bump_candidate` skips any PR that is handed over or has no tracking issue, then takes the oldest that may merge, or else the oldest. `decide()` still re-derives everything from the job's own fresh fetch (FR-003). Test: an older unverified PR plus a newer verified one must pick the newer.
4. **Transient merge failures were classed `other` and handed over for good.** Fixed. There is a new `transient` refusal class: head or base moved, 5xx, mergeability still being computed, merge already in progress. It is checked after `workflow-scope`, so a missing workflow scope is never called transient. The merge step retries once, but only after re-fetching the snapshot and re-deriving the decision; the retry is pinned to the head that new decision names. If the head moved, the result is `not-merged`. A second transient failure is announced as `transient`, with no handover and no `handed-over` marker. For a bump PR, the next run re-evaluates it; for a fix PR, readiness's awaiting-merge hand-off stays in place. Test: the gate requires head-moved, base-moved, 502 and 503 stderr to classify as retryable, and requires the merge step to call `board_merge.py retryable`. There is a `refusal-transient.json` fixture, and `refusal-other.json` (which was a 502) is now a real "not accessible by integration" error. I also ran the merge and announce steps against a stub `gh`: merged, transient-then-merged, transient-twice and refused each give the expected outcome and marker.
5. **`verification_passed_at_head` used only the latest bot record.** Fixed. Only records at the fresh head count, so a late record for an old head can't void a valid one. Among this head's own records the latest still wins (data-model.md), ordered by createdAt and then the numeric comment id, so two records in the same second always sort the same way. On "fooled by bot-quoted text": quoted stderr and paths are defanged (`<!--` is broken up), so an App announcement can't carry a forged marker. Tests: `bump-pass-late-record-for-old-head.json`, `bump-verification_passed_at_head-same-second.json`, and a gate check that a marker quoted from stderr doesn't become a record.
6. **The verification record was posted after PR creation with no retry.** Fixed. The record is posted before the issue comment and retried three times (0, 5 and 15 s apart). If all three fail, the step fails loudly and the issue says the PR awaits a human merge; re-running wouldn't help, because preflight declines a candidate that already has a PR. I also bound the record to `git rev-parse refs/heads/$BRANCH`, the commit actually verified and pushed. The old code re-read the PR's head, and a push after `gh pr create` could have bound a pass to an unverified commit. Tests: S5 now asserts the record names the pushed commit, and the new S5b injects one failed `gh pr comment` (a new `GH_STUB_FAIL_ONCE` option in the stub). While doing this I found S5 was already failing locally at 94f63b5, because `GITHUB_RUN_ID` was unbound under `set -u`. `new_step_env` now defaults it.
7. **The merge job requests `actions: write` it may not need.** Refuted, plus a guard. `github.token` is passed as the kill-switch re-check's `cancel-token`, and `wing-commander-board-stop-check` runs `gh run cancel` and the run read with it. The App token has no `actions` permission (#461; see the composite's header). Every other job that calls the composite grants `actions: write` for the same reason. The job now has a comment saying so. The finding's second half was valid: `verify-board-merge.py` now pins the merge job's permissions to exactly `contents: read, issues: write, pull-requests: read, actions: write`, so `github.token` can never be widened enough to merge or push. Its self-test fails a `contents: write` variant.
8. **The single-merge-call check used text membership.** Fixed. `merge_calls_outside()` now goes by the merge job's line span instead of the line's text, so an identical line pasted into another job is caught. Test: a self-test workflow with that pasted line, which the old check passed.

### Other tasks

- **T028 / MF005:** `verify-constitution-merge-class-parity.py` now requires `WING_COMMANDER_BOARD_AUTO_MERGE` in both places, in both directions:
  - a board-loop `gh pr merge` that isn't gated on the switch fails;
  - Principle X naming the switch while board-loop.yml never gates on it fails;
  - a gated merge that Principle X doesn't name fails.

  Seven new self-test cases cover this. **The constitution doesn't name the switch yet,** and per the spec 114 precedent a lifecycle PR carries no `.specify/memory/` edit. The second is a Spec Kit upgrade PR from the auto-update stage, merged once its assigned verification passed on that SHA and the gate suite is green; the backstop does not apply to it. The decision is made by deterministic code in `.github/scripts/board_merge.py`, which re-derives every condition from a freshly fetched snapshot of the head SHA. The merge is a squash pinned to that SHA, and each merge or refusal is announced on the PR and the issue. A refusal, such as a missing Workflows scope on a workflow-touching PR, is handed to a maintainer with GitHub's reason and never routed around. Actions-only behaviour changes get a post-merge prove entry. The change adds a `merge` job to `board-loop.yml`, a new gate `verify-board-merge.py` with per-condition fixtures, and a verification record written by the auto-update act job. ⚠️ **Not fully converged — 14 tasks remain**

This specification, 117 (implement stall hand-off and honest remaining-work reporting), changes how the pipeline reports unfinished work. Before it, a lifecycle could stop in implement with work outstanding and the final PR would blur owner-only steps together with code that still needed building. Tasks marked `[maintainer]` (for example, a workflow re-drive or a post-merge proof) are now classified separately from implementation tasks, so implement and its loop ignore them rather than treating them as blockers. Standing instructions such as "Keep the gates green" are excluded from the counts, and each unchecked line is classified once by a shared script, `count-tasks-checkboxes.sh`.

The implement loop now stops only when continuing cannot help. It reads a validated `implement-blocker.json` written by the agent (closed `kind` list, single-line sanitised `detail`, and a `task` id that must be an unchecked implementation task at the pushed tip), and a pure decision script, `decide-implement-outcome.sh`, chooses between converged, progressed, and hand-off. A hand-off or a cap with implementation outstanding posts a stall comment on the lifecycle issue that states the outstanding count and the reason. Both the primary and retry arms of `implement.yml` call the same scripts.

Finalize renders its remaining-work report deterministically through `render-remaining-work.sh`, with separate "Maintainer steps" and "Unfinished implementation" sections and a stall statement when implementation remains. The summarising agent no longer copies task lines by hand. Re-entry from review is also made explicit: a manual dispatch on a review-stage lifecycle comments why nothing ran, and the Maintainer Feedback cycle start comment reports how many cycles remain. A new gate, `verify-implement-stall-handoff.py`, runs fixtures for each shared script and checks the workflow wiring. Several existing gates were fixed along the way (gates 24, fold-dispatch-once, project-single-home, intake-routing). Five rounds of review findings were folded in; some items from rounds 4 and 5 remain open and are listed below.

## Local finish: lint made green on `spec/117-implement-stall-handoff` (2597c63)

The lifecycle is past its implement cap and the review gate stands down on a red head, so this was finished locally per the standing decision (#990, #994, #903). Started from 93ae94a9.

### What was failing
The `lint` check on 902aa6f and 93ae94a: one real gate failure from the round-2 fixes.

- **`verify-single-home-idioms.py`**: `.github/actions/wing-commander-remaining-work/action.yml` read `impl_count="$(cat … || echo 0)"`. That puts the fallback inside the command substitution, where it appends to the output instead of replacing it (the #889/#959 idiom).

Three other gates failed in the local suite but are not defects:
- `verify-truncated-cycle-carry-forward.py`: load-sensitive; passes when run alone.
- `verify-auto-release-gate-waits-for-stage.py`: load-sensitive; passes when run alone.
- Gate 62 and its self-test: fail only because the container has no Docker; waived.

### Fixes
1. **Idiom fix.** The fallback now sits on the assignment: `impl_count="$(cat …)" || impl_count=0`. No behaviour change.
2. **`review-step-gating` pass (T027e).** Gate 24 and `stranded-steps.py` report no new findings in `implement.yml` or `finalize.yml` compared with the merge base. Reading the new steps by hand turned up one real defect in the `wing-commander-remaining-work` composite:
   - **The defect:** the render step runs without `-e`. If `render-remaining-work.sh` failed, the step still succeeded, leaving an empty `finalize-remaining.md` and `stalled=false`. `Verify agent output` saw the file exist, so finalize would open the PR and announce "No manual work remains" even with implementation outstanding. That breaks FR-008.
   - **The fix:** on a render failure the composite logs `::error::`, removes the partial report and exits 0. `Verify agent output` then fails on the missing file and the `always()`-gated "Announce finalize failure" callout fires. Because the step doesn't hard-fail, it can't strand that path.
   - **The test:** Gate 165 (`verify-implement-stall-handoff.py`) now runs the composite's `run:` block twice, once with the real renderer and once with a renderer that fails. The failing-renderer case fails on the pre-fix composite (empty report, `stalled=false`) and passes with the fix.
3. **tasks.md:** T027, T027e and T027f are checked off. T029 and T030 stay maintainer steps.

### Gate result
`python .github/scripts/run-local-gates.py --jobs 4` passes 271 of 274 gates. The three failures are the Docker-only Gate 62 pair and `verify-auto-release-gate-waits-for-stage.py`, which passes when re-run alone. Gate 165 passes all 243 cases.

This specification makes the two review loops, `lifecycle-review-gate.yml` and `board-loop.yml`, notice when they are not converging. A new shared module, `.github/scripts/wc_convergence.py`, now holds all of the convergence arithmetic: attribution by blame, churn, growth, the recurrence check against the folded-fingerprint ledger, and the decision that stops a loop. The `review-until-clean` skill's `thrash_signals.py` is a thin caller of that module and keeps its flags and `--self-test`. A new gate, `verify-convergence-single-home.py`, fails if a copy of that arithmetic or a duplicate threshold reappears in a workflow, composite or skill script. Its failure branches each have a checked-in fixture.

A finding that re-appears after it was folded or fixed is now classified as a recurrence. It keeps the round from resolving clean, posts no success status, and is named on the lifecycle issue or the PR. This removes the false green seen in #833. From round 3, a loop whose signals trip (count not falling, self-inflicted share, recurrence, churn streak or growth) stops with the `not-converging` stall reason, uses the standard hand-off, and leaves the PR open and unmerged. The round budget is unchanged and still takes precedence. Replay fixtures from the #833, #954 and #969 histories, and per-rule trip fixtures, back these behaviours in `.github/scripts/wc_convergence_tests/`.

The fold-time analyze check (User Story 3, tasks T020–T027) was split out to proposal #1066 at the owner's decision on 2026-10-19 and is not part of this branch. Its tasks are marked as moved rather than done. Review findings that cite only that code were handled the same way. Tasks T001–T019 and T028–T030 are complete. Story 5 is out of scope under FR-020.

Two owner decisions from 2026-10-21 are built on this branch. Both make the loops survive `rebase.yml` rewriting the branch on every push to main:

- **Growth survives a rebase (F2 (b)).** Each round record stores the reviewed head's diff size (`diff_lines`). When earlier round heads can no longer be resolved, `compute_history` reads growth from those stored sizes. Self-inflicted share and churn read n/a after a rebase, and the hand-off says so (spec Edge Case). A head that is not an ancestor of the next one is treated as rewritten history, so the PR's own lines are never blamed on the loop. The root fix, an opt-in merge-from-main sync, is #1074.
- **A rebase alone doesn't re-arm a stopped loop (FR-008).** Each round record also stores a fingerprint of the PR's own diff (`diff_fp`, a `git patch-id --verbatim` of the diff against the merge base). After a `not-converging` stop, the lifecycle review gate selects the PR again only when that fingerprint changes. So a rebase or a merge of main does not re-arm the review, and a push that changes the PR's code does. Records without a fingerprint fall back to the old head-moved rule. The board loop's not-converging stall already waits for a human to remove `board:stalled`.

Later review passes also hardened the module:
- the round record and the hand-off are bounded by their encoded size;
- git output is read as bytes and split on `\n` only, so non-UTF-8 files and odd separators can neither crash the evaluate step nor shift blame;
- line-ending-only and whitespace-only pushes move the fingerprint;
- reviewer-supplied paths in the hand-off are fenced;
- lint-workflows now triggers on the skill scripts that Gate 165 scans.

## Summary

Draft specification for **spec 118 — keep spec branches current by merging main (sync-from-main)**.

Today every push to `main` rebases each in-flight `spec/*` branch and force-pushes it, so every branch SHA changes and the old ones leave the remote. That breaks spec 116's convergence signals (share, churn), finalize's fold range and fold log (#918, #1068), and SHAs recorded on PRs and issues.

The spec adds a second sync method that merges `main` into the branch with a sync commit and never force-pushes:

- **Selection**: one repository switch (`rebase` | `merge`), unset = `rebase`; read by the wrapper and passed to the stage as a declared input (constitution VII).
- **Naming**: reads as syncing ("sync-from-main" / "Sync spec branch with main"), never as a feature merge.
- **Conflicts**: same model as rebase: agent resolution, deterministic scope check before publish, escalation on the lifecycle issue.
- **Payoff**: history-derived consumers keep resolving recorded SHAs and exclude sync-commit changes from the lifecycle's own diff.

All clarifications are resolved (answers on #1074, recorded in the spec's Clarifications section):

1. FR-012: the switch is read at run time; every in-flight branch uses the new method from the next push to `main`.
2. FR-013: squash-merging of final PRs is a documented assumption only; merge sync adds no coupling to the final-merge method.
3. FR-014: the rebase path keeps #1062's stored per-round diff size, adds no new workarounds, and reports other history-derived signals as n/a with a "rebase rewrites history; merge sync avoids it" reason.

Spec: `specs/118-spec-branch-sync-from-main/spec.md`

Closes nothing — lifecycle issue: #1074

## Summary

Spec 119 re-specifies spec 116's Story 3 (FR-011–FR-017) as a much smaller design: **one lifecycle hold label** instead of a hold-and-release protocol.

- **The hold (P1)**: a single label (default `lifecycle:held`), distinct from `stage:stalled`, read by implement at the start of every cycle and by `wing-commander-fold-dispatch`. While it is set, nothing is built or dispatched. It can be set by hand, by a maintainer's strict `stop`/`/stop` on the lifecycle issue or PR (reusing `board_stop_check.py`'s parser), or by fold-time analyze. Removing the label releases it, in any repository.
- **Fold-time analyze (P2)**: a read-only Sonnet job between fold commit and dispatch. It sees only the fold's own tasks.md diff. A deterministic decide step holds only on a well-formed constitution conflict.
- **Release paths (P2)**: proceed, drop, amend and retry, each through an existing path. No `/fold-hold` command, no release stage, no markers, no lock. A dropped task's findings reach spec 116's convergence signals as dismissed.

All clarifications are resolved (owner's answers on #1066): only the strict `stop`/`/stop` form sets the hold, and pr-conversation's classified `stop` reply tells the maintainer how to set it; a drop's dismissal is derived from the fold task's removal from tasks.md, with no new state; the comment and amendment-PR answer paths are sufficient. See the spec's Clarifications section.

Depends on spec 116's convergence stories (#1062) for the dismissed-fingerprint set.

Closes nothing — lifecycle issue: #1066

## What & why

**#1054.** `metrics-persist.yml`'s sweep listed its window with one filtered `actions/runs` call.
- GitHub returns at most 1,000 runs for such a listing, newest first, and this repository passes that in a day.
- The oldest runs were silently dropped, never written to `unpersisted.jsonl`, and the high-water mark advanced past them.
- On 2026-10-15 that lost 20 runs' records: 7 implement, 2 finalize, 1 watchdog and 10 board-loop runs.

**The fix** is in "Resolve the sweep window and list its runs":
- **Re-listing:** a listing that reaches the cap is listed again, with the `created` range closed at the oldest creation time it saw. This repeats until a listing comes back under the cap. Each listing still uses `--paginate` and the same per-item `--jq` (Gate 18).
- **Duplicates:** slices share their boundary second, so runs are de-duplicated by `run_id` before the existing window, skip and allowlist filters. The `created_at` field used for narrowing is stripped before `sweep-runs`.
- **Fail closed:** a listing that cannot be narrowed (1,000 or more runs created in one second) fails the step as not-collected, the same way a failed listing does today. The mark is never advanced over runs the sweep didn't see.

**Tests, in Gate 77 (`verify-metrics-sweep-high-water-mark.py`):**
- **Stub:** the harness's gh stub now behaves like the API. It honours the `created` range, orders newest first and caps at 1,000.
- **New scenarios:** a 2,037-run window, which must list every run exactly once, and a 1,000-runs-in-one-second window, which must fail.
- **New mutations:** "one capped listing and nothing more" (the pre-fix behaviour) and "a stuck cap accepted". The gate catches both.

**Not in this PR:** recovering the 2026-10-14 and 10-15 runs. Their artifacts have likely expired; if they can still be read, a manual `since` dispatch of the sweep would collect them.

## Checks

- [x] For workflow changes: `actionlint` passes; it is part of the gate suite.
- [x] No credentials or tokens in the diff.

`python .github/scripts/run-local-gates.py --jobs 4`: 275/277 pass. The two that fail are `verify-gate-62.py` and its `--self-test`, which need a Docker daemon (waived).

## What & why

**#999 is a real production race, not a flaky test.**

**Where.** Both implement read-back steps decide whether an exhausted cycle made outside-spec progress with this check (Arm B):

    git log -E --format='%H' --author=... "$BASE_SHA..origin/<spec branch>" ... -- . ":(exclude)$SPEC_DIR/**" | grep -q .

**Why it flips.** These steps run under `bash -eo pipefail`.
- `git log` flushes after each commit, and `grep -q .` exits on the first hash.
- With two or more qualifying commits, `grep` can exit before git's next write. git then takes SIGPIPE and exits 141.
- `pipefail` turns the `if` false. Arm B reads "no progress", and an exhausted cycle that only made code commits is escalated or stalled instead of carried forward.
- On a runner this is more likely, not less, because real branches have many agent commits.

**Evidence, from a diagnosis run on 2026-10-22:**
- **Idle:** Gate 30 scenario 4d passed 30/30.
- **Under CPU load:** with 4 parallel copies, 9/100 failed. Every failure had the issue's exact message: `expected ok='true', got 'false'`.
- **Bare pipeline, real git, under load:** `PIPESTATUS [141 0]` in 10/400 runs.
- **With a shim that paces `git log` output:** it fails 5/5. The single-commit control passes.

**The fix.** In both "Read back cycle outcome" and "Read back retry outcome", the check is now `[ -n "$(git log -1 … )" ]`. There is no pipe to break. A failing `git log` still gives an empty substitution, so it still reads as false.

**Tests, in Gate 30 (`verify-truncated-cycle-carry-forward.py`):**
- **Shim:** a paced-git shim (git log output one line per 0.3 s, reporting 141 when its reader leaves, as real git does) makes the race deterministic.
- **Scenario 4e:** 4d run under the shim. It must give ok=true and truncated=true.
- **Retry check:** `check_retry_arm_b_paced_git` puts two Arm-B commits on the retry path, under the shim.
- **Both fail without the fix:** with `implement.yml` reverted to main, 4e gives `ok='false'`, `truncated='false'` and the retry check gives `ok='false'`. Both pass with it.
- **Mutation:** the Arm-B widening mutation follows the new text.

## Checks

- [x] For workflow changes: `actionlint` passes; it is part of the gate suite.
- [x] No credentials or tokens in the diff.

`python .github/scripts/run-local-gates.py --jobs 4`: 275/277 pass. The two that fail are `verify-gate-62.py` and its `--self-test`, which need a Docker daemon (waived).

**Related:** the same `| grep -q` shape, at lower risk, in `board-loop.yml` and `wing-commander-9-pr-conversation.yml`, is a Maintenance backlog line on #889, not part of this PR.

## What & why

This fixes the four #889 Maintenance backlog lines that must be fixed before `WING_COMMANDER_BOARD_AUTO_MERGE` is enabled (spec 115, board-loop self-merge). The live contract `specs/115-board-loop-self-merge/contracts/board-merge.md` is updated to match. `decide()` is still pure.

The fallback that accepted a self-asserted `<slug>[bot]@users.noreply.github.com` email for an empty login is removed. I checked against the live API: the auto-update stage's existing plain noreply email already resolves to the bot account, so the stage needs no change. <!-- wing-commander-finalize:narrative:begin -->
This specification adds a merge-based way to keep spec branches current with `main`, selected by one switch. Until now the `rebase` workflow rewrote a spec branch onto `main` and force-pushed it. The new `merge` arm in `.github/workflows/rebase.yml` instead records a single two-parent sync commit (`sync: merge <default> into <spec-branch>`) and publishes it with a plain fast-forward push, so no earlier commit is rewritten. The switch is the repository variable `WING_COMMANDER_SPEC_BRANCH_SYNC`, which takes `rebase` (the default and unchanged behaviour) or `merge`; any other value fails the discover job before a branch is touched. The helper `.github/scripts/wc_sync_from_main.py` owns method validation, the up-to-date decision, the publish refspec, and the deterministic scope check that decides whether a conflict resolution may be published or must be escalated.

Conflicts under `merge` follow the same path as the rebase arm. An agent resolves the conflict with a restricted tool list, and `verify-scope` then checks that the resolved tree changes only admitted paths, that no conflict markers remain, that HEAD has the expected two parents, and that the verdict is healthy. Failures escalate with the existing `rebase:blocked` label and marker, using merge-specific prose. The metrics, execution-log, and cost-line steps are shared with the rebase arm rather than copied. A new gate, `verify-sync-from-main.py`, covers the helper with git-fixture tests and is registered in `lint-workflows.yml`.

The history consumers were made merge-aware. Convergence signals in `wc_convergence.py` attribute commits reachable from the sync commit's second parent to `base` rather than to a review pass, and report an explicit n/a reason on the rebase path. Documentation in `docs/adoption.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/setup.md` describes the switch, its squash-merge assumption, and the trade-off against stable history. Review rounds 1 to 4 each folded their findings into the branch, and the implementation checklist is complete. Three maintainer steps remain: merging the implementation PR with a `workflow`-scoped token, setting the variable on a test repository and dispatching a sync, and post-merge proof on the lifecycle issue.

> ## Question 1
> 
> **Context**: FR-012 / Edge Cases
> 
> **What we need to know**: Can a repository switch between rebase and merge sync while lifecycles are in flight, and if so how are branches already rebased (or already carrying sync commits) treated?
> 
> **Suggested Answers**:
> 
> | Option | Answer | Implications |
> |--------|--------|--------------|
> | A | Allowed; the new method applies to every in-flight branch on the next push to main | Simplest. A lifecycle that started under rebase keeps its already-broken recorded SHAs, but stays stable from the switch on; switching merge→rebase would linearize away the sync commits. |
> | B | Allowed; each lifecycle is pinned to the method it started under (recorded in spec-meta.json) | No lifecycle sees a mid-flight change in history semantics; needs a per-lifecycle record and both paths live at once until old lifecycles drain. |
> | C | Refused while any lifecycle is open; the run fails loudly naming the open lifecycles | Strongest guarantee, but blocks the switch in a busy repository until the board drains. |
> | Custom | Provide your own answer | Reply on this issue with your own answer |
> 
> **Your choice**: _Reply on this issue_
> 
> ## Question 2
> 
> **Context**: FR-013 / Assumptions
> 
> **What we need to know**: Final PRs are squash-merged today, so sync commits never reach main. How should merge sync depend on that?
> 
> **Suggested Answers**:
> 
> | Option | Answer | Implications |
> |--------|--------|--------------|
> | A | Documented assumption only | No new code; if a repository stops squash-merging, sync merge commits land on main. |
> | B | Enforced: merge sync (or finalize) refuses unless the final PR will be squash-merged | Deterministic guarantee that main never receives sync commits; adds a check and couples merge sync to the final-merge method. |
> | C | Acceptable either way: sync commits on main are fine if squash-merging ever stops | No coupling, but main history would gain merge commits from spec branches in that case. |
> | Custom | Provide your own answer | Reply on this issue with your own answer |
> 
> **Your choice**: _Reply on this issue_
> 
> ## Question 3
> 
> **Context**: FR-014 / User Story 4
> 
> **What we need to know**: Under the rebase method, should the rebase path keep its own workarounds for history-derived signals (e.g. #1062's stored per-round diff size), or report those signals as n/a with an explicit reason?
> 
> **Suggested Answers**:
> 
> | Option | Answer | Implications |
> |--------|--------|--------------|
> | A | Keep existing workarounds and add more where feasible | Rebase adopters keep the most signal; more code to maintain on a path merge sync makes unnecessary. |
> | B | Keep existing workarounds (e.g. stored diff size) but add no new ones; report the rest as n/a with a 'rebase rewrites history; use merge sync' reason | No regression for current adopters, bounded maintenance, clear pointer to the fix. |
> | C | Remove the workarounds; under rebase every history-derived signal reads n/a with that reason | Simplest code; rebase adopters lose growth, which #1062 currently preserves. |
> | Custom | Provide your own answer | Reply on this issue with your own answer |

Spec 118 (sync-from-main) adds a second way to keep in-flight `spec/*` branches current: merging the default branch into the branch with a sync commit, instead of rebasing onto it. The choice is made by the repository variable `WING_COMMANDER_SPEC_BRANCH_SYNC` (`rebase` remains the default, `merge` opts in), which the wrapper passes to the existing `rebase.yml` stage as a typed `sync-method` input. A merge sync never rewrites history and publishes with a plain fast-forward push, so it cannot clobber a branch that moved meanwhile.

All merge-sync decisions live in a new deterministic helper, `wc_sync_from_main.py`, and a git-fixture gate, `verify-sync-from-main.py`, exercises every failure branch and mutation-tests the scope checks. A conflicting merge still goes to the same agent, and its result is checked against the `git merge-tree` tree so that only conflicting paths may differ. Failures abort the merge and escalate through the existing `rebase:blocked` label. History readers (`wc_convergence.py` and the finalize fold range) now attribute main-side commits to the base and state why a signal is unknowable after a rebase. The stage's contract and the architecture and setup docs are updated to match.

Maintenance backlog (#889) line: implement's gate-suite steps have a 10-minute step timeout.

## Why
#1077 fixed the cycle-start gate job's pipeline checkout (#1071). Spec 118's first implement cycle after it, [run 40101571746](https://github.com/charlesguse/wing-commander/actions/runs/40101571746), was the first run since 10-15 in which the cycle-start suite actually ran. In the 29 runs sampled before it, that step was skipped. The suite then hit its 10-minute step timeout (14:14:44 to 14:24:44). The step was killed before the composite uploaded a verdict, so the implement job read "gate verdict absent" and started the cycle red. Locally the full suite now takes 10–17 minutes with `--jobs 4`.

## What
- Both implement suite steps (the credential-free cycle-start job and the in-job retry) get `timeout-minutes: 30`.
- `wing-commander-contained-gate-suite` gains an optional `suite-timeout-minutes` input (default `50`, below the board loop's 60-minute steps; implement passes `25`). `_shared/contained-gate-suite.sh` runs the suite under `timeout`. A suite still running when the budget runs out is stopped, and the verdict is `fail` with "gate suite did not finish within its time budget". The failure is named before the step timeout can drop the upload. Without `timeout` on the image, the step timeout still applies, as it does today.
- The summary step in both legs no longer ends "first failure: " with nothing after it. With no failure line, it says none was recorded.

## Tests
- Gate 155 (`verify-gate-bundle-roundtrip.py`) drives a suite past a 2-second budget and expects a named fail verdict. Two mutations check it: no budget, and a stopped suite reported as an ordinary failure.
- `verify-implement-gate-suite-preflight.py` adds two checks: both legs' suite steps allow ≥ 30 minutes, and the composite's budget sits below the cycle step's. Run against main's `implement.yml`, the gate refuses on the new summary mutation. It also adds a summary scenario for an empty failure line, plus that mutation, in both legs.
- Full suite: 275/277. The two failures are Gate 62 and its self-test, which need Docker (a known local-only failure, #889).

snapshot.body:
Fixes the daily auto-release failure tracked on #1083 (failing every day since 2026-10-25).

## Root cause

#1077 made this repository's implement wrapper pass `pipeline-ref: ${{ github.sha }}`. Here that's right, because the wrapper calls `implement.yml` by local path. `auto-release.yml`'s scaffold step and `provision-e2e-target.sh` copy that wrapper into the test repository but rewrite only its `uses:` line. In the test repository, `github.sha` is the test repository's own commit.

Every job in implement then failed its pipeline checkout. Scratch run 41421061965, implement job:

```
fetch --depth=1 origin ee775e7ed40fbdbf890a47f264c96aad2a586a30
fatal: remote error: upload-pack: not our ref ee775e7ed40fbdbf890a47f264c96aad2a586a30
```

`ee775e7` is the scratch repository's merge commit for its spec PR. Each nightly lifecycle stayed in `stage:tasks` until the 8100s poll budget ran out. The gate-suite job looked green because its checkout step is allowed to fail and the suite was skipped.

Consumers are unaffected: #1077 is not in any release (v2.7.16 predates it), and the wrapper snippets in `docs/adoption.md` don't set `pipeline-ref`.

## Change

- New `.github/actions/_shared/pin-e2e-wrapper.sh` is the one home of the e2e wrapper pin. It rewrites the stage call, and it also rewrites `pipeline-ref: ${{ github.sha }}` to the pipeline commit. It refuses (exit 1) a wrapper that either rewrite missed, so a reformatted line can't silently no-op.
- `auto-release.yml`'s scaffold step and `provision-e2e-target.sh` call it in place of their two inline sed copies. In auto-release, a refusal becomes a `fail-infra` verdict.
- The E2E provisioning single-home gate:
  - fails when either caller stops using the script, or when an inline `uses: ./.github/workflows/` sed reappears;
  - runs the real script over every wrapper the scaffold copies, and fails on any pinned `pipeline-ref` other than the pinned commit.
  - New self-test mutations: (d) drop the script's pipeline-ref rewrite, so the implement wrapper must fail; (e) paste the old inline sed back, which must fail.
- `verify-auto-release-e2e-pin.py`'s "pin tag, never the bare head" check now reads the script call rather than the old sed text.

## Validation

- Gate suite: 273/277. The 4 failures were:
  - Gate 62 and its self-test: need Docker, the known local waiver.
  - `verify-single-home-idioms` and `verify-auto-release-e2e-pin`: real, both fixed in f1b0c63. Re-ran every gate matching auto-release, comment-canonical, single-home and e2e, and all passed.
- With `auto-release.yml` and `provision-e2e-target.sh` reverted to main, the single-home gate fails, naming both missing calls and both inline seds.
- Proof after merge: the next nightly auto-release run should take the scratch lifecycle past implement's pipeline checkout.

## Summary

Draft spec `specs/121-board-backlog-line-items/` lets the board loop take **one unchecked Maintenance backlog line** as its work item when no eligible issue is waiting.

- **P1**: An idle loop claims one line, runs the same triage, route, fix, review, readiness and merge steps as for an issue (the line's text stands in for the issue body), and ticks the line with "(fixed by #PR)" when the fix merges. The backlog issue is never closed.

- **P2**: A line the loop can't finish is held with the same reason a `board:stalled` issue would get, and selection skips it.
- **P1**: Every edit to the backlog is a read-modify-write that changes only the one line and keeps concurrent edits from other writers.

Defaults in Assumptions: the loop takes lines only when the issue queue is empty. A bundled line is worked as one item, bounded by the existing backstop. Plan should confirm that Principle X's entry rule covers a line on a backlog issue that a maintainer authored.

Spec 120 makes runs that the pipeline dispatches with the workflow's built-in token persist their own prompt-metrics records. Before this change, those runs fire no `workflow_run` event, so their records waited for the daily sweep. Implement and finalize now each end with a `persist-metrics` job that calls the existing `metrics-persist.yml` reusable workflow. The job runs in the same run as the stage, so records reach the metrics branch without depending on the completion trigger.

The reusable workflow gained two opt-in inputs, both defaulting to `false` so existing callers behave exactly as before. `run-in-cancelled-run` lets the persist step run after a cancelled run, so spend from a run cancelled mid-cycle is still recorded. `tolerate-failure` keeps a metrics failure from changing the run's conclusion, and a warning step names the daily sweep as the backstop. The metrics-persist composite action now de-duplicates records on a key that stays stable across re-run attempts, so a record persisted by the stage job, the `workflow_run` path and the sweep appears once. The rollup renders a "Last daily sweep" line that says `unknown` when no sweep has run.

Finalize does not gate its persist job on a "something started" signal. Research R2's planned early `started` output was not built; the owner chose the fallback, so a run cancelled while queued still starts the persist job, where the zero-record path makes it a no-op. The finalize wrapper comment and `contracts/persisting-job.md` record this as a measured exception to FR-011. Implement's persist job waits for the whole implement call, including any queued `stalled` job, so persistence can be delayed by that job; this is also recorded as an accepted exception.

Gate 79 (`verify-metrics-wrapper-trigger-drops-watchdog.py`) now checks the persisting jobs in both wrappers, the input defaults, the absence of App-token secrets and `concurrency:` keys, and that the stage-side `workflow_run` and sweep jobs do not pass the new inputs. Each failure branch has a fixture. The contracts that the new behaviour changes (`persisting-job.md`, `wrapper-contract.md`, `persist-workflow.md`, `metrics-persist-sweep-delta.md`) were amended to match. Three rounds of review findings were folded in, and the fixes are recorded in `tasks.md`.

What the code does not yet prove is behaviour that only a real Actions run can show: the record reaching the metrics branch, cancellation handling, the unwritable-destination warning, and the no-duplicate check after re-runs. Those are maintainer drills, and they are not part of this change's verified state.

Spec 120 (dispatched-run metrics, lifecycle #1055) makes implement and finalize runs write their own metrics records. Runs dispatched with the built-in token never fire the metrics `workflow_run` trigger, so their records used to wait for the daily sweep. Each wrapper now has a `persist-metrics` job that calls the existing `metrics-persist.yml` stage with the run's own id, with no App credentials and no concurrency group. Two optional, default-off stage inputs let it run in a cancelled run and keep it from failing the origin run. snapshot.body:
Fixes the container-mode half of #1083 (auto-release run 41806089944, 2026-11-04).

## Root cause

The test lifecycle finished. In charlesguse/wing-commander-auto-release-scratch#167, final PR #171 merged at 09:29:48, and cleanup then:
- closed the issue at 09:31:20, with `gh issue close --comment`;
- labelled it `stage:done` at 09:31:22.

The auto-release poll read the issue in that two-second gap and filed:

```
Classification: pipeline defect (fail-incomplete)
Observed: state=CLOSED labels=[spec-request,stage:review,spec:022-release-verification-doc]
```

The poll treated any `CLOSED` read as terminal, so it never re-read. Cleanup's close-then-label order is deliberate: the close carries the summary comment in one call, and labelling first would leave an issue that is open but marked `stage:done` if the close then failed. So the fix belongs in the poll.

## Change

- **`auto-release.yml` poll step:** a closed issue carrying neither `stage:done` nor `stage:stalled` is re-read for up to `MAX_CLOSED_SETTLE_POLLS=4` more polls (30 s apart) before it counts as terminal. One that never gains `stage:done` still ends `fail-incomplete`, as before.
- **Gate 115 (`verify-auto-release-poll-credential-failure.py`)** already runs the real poll step against a stubbed `gh`. It gains:
  - a `view_sequence_stub` that replays `gh issue view` answers;
  - three scenarios:
    - control: closed with `stage:done` at once;
    - race: closed with `stage:review`, then `stage:done`. It must reach the control's verdict;
    - never done: must still end `fail-incomplete`, naming `stage:review`.
  - a mutation that drops the settle window, which the race scenario must catch.

## Validation

- With `auto-release.yml` reverted to main, Gate 115 fails the race scenario with `outcome: fail-incomplete … state=CLOSED labels=[stage:review]`, exactly what happened on 2026-11-04. With the fix it passes: 6 scenarios, 3 mutations, 0 failures.
- Full gate suite: 275/277. The 2 failures are Gate 62 and its self-test, which need Docker (known local waiver).
- Proof after merge: the next container-mode auto-release run. #1083 closes once that run passes.

Fixes the two defects behind #1094's stall on 2026-11-03 (clarify run 41579024064), which the board loop routed to spec proposals #1099 and #1103. Both are deterministic fixes with a gate behind them, so they don't need a spec.

## #1099: a quoted marker vetoed a finished spec

The colon-form marker scan in `intake.yml` and `clarify.yml` was `grep -q '\[NEEDS CLARIFICATION:' spec.md`. Spec 122 is *about* the clarification marker, so its text quotes the marker in backticks. After the owner answered every question, clarify reported none open, but the scan found the quotes, vetoed the readiness callout and failed the run, stalling the lifecycle.

The scan now strips fenced code blocks and inline code spans before grepping:

```bash
if sed -e '/^[[:space:]]*```/,/^[[:space:]]*```/d' -e 's/`[^`]*`//g' "$SPEC_DIR/spec.md" | grep -q '\[NEEDS CLARIFICATION:'; then
```

A real marker, written as Spec Kit's template writes it, outside code, still blocks as before. The scan is one line that the two stages carry identically, and the gate now checks they stay identical.

## #1103: clarify's stall notice checked out a branch that doesn't exist yet

Clarify's stalled job passed `spec-branch: spec/<slug>` to `wing-commander-chain-stop-notice` so it could mark the lifecycle record stalled. Before the spec PR merges, the spec lives on `spec-draft/<slug>`, and `spec/<slug>` doesn't exist. So the checkout failed on every clarify stall (the `missing-spec-branch` annotation), and the notice said the record "could not be updated".

Clarify now passes `spec-dir: ""`, as intake already does (research.md D5): there is no record to mark before the merge. Marking the draft's record instead would carry `stage: stalled` into the spec when its PR merges. The two steps that only fed that call (independent slug and spec-dir re-derivation) are removed.

## Tests

`verify-clarification-gating.py` now has:
- a scenario per stage: a spec that quotes the marker only in code and has no open questions must announce ready and stay green;
- a structural check that both stages' marker scans are the same one line that strips code;
- a structural check that clarify's chain-stop-notice call passes `spec-dir: ""` and no `spec-branch`;
- a mutation that restores the plain grep. The quoted-marker scenarios must break under it, and they do (4 assertions).

With `intake.yml` and `clarify.yml` reverted to main, the gate fails all four new checks for the reasons they name. With the fix: 28 scenarios, 0 failures.

Full gate suite: 275/277. The two failures are Gate 62 and its self-test, which need Docker (known local waiver).

## After merge

Close #1099 and #1103 as fixed here. Proof comes with the next clarify run on a spec that quotes the marker, or the next clarify stall, whichever comes first.
